title: Le lendemain matin chez ASK  (The Morning After at ASK)

segments.t: It is Monday morning at the ASK agency after an eventful weekend. Andrea walks in feeling energized, while Gabriel arrives exhausted after two days in custody with Norman. Listen to the scene in French first. Don't worry about catching every word.
Bonjour, Arlette.
Bonjour, Andréa. Tu as bien dormi?
Arlette, cette herbe est terrible.
J'ai fait des rêves érotiques dingues tout le week-end.
Pas moi.
Pourquoi tu n'es pas venu à la fête?
J'avais des obligations personnelles.
Des obligations personnelles un dimanche soir?
Une affaire urgente avec un talent.
Salut tout le monde. Ça va, Marteau?
Ça va très bien!
Et pour Aymeline Val aussi!
C'était pas dingue ce projet?
C'était dingue!
Au moins, tout le monde est là ce matin.
Let's walk through the lively morning exchange at ASK step by step.
Bonjour, Arlette.
'Good morning, Arlette.' Even on a Monday morning, French uses one all-purpose 'good day' greeting rather than a separate 'good morning'.
Bonjour, Andréa. Tu as bien dormi?
'Good morning, Andrea. Did you sleep well?' Sliding 'well' between 'have' and 'slept'—literally 'you have well slept?'—is natural French word order.
Arlette, cette herbe est terrible.
'Arlette, that weed is killer.' Slang flips the cognate 'terrible' upside down so it can mean 'awesome', 'potent', or 'killer' in casual French!
J'ai fait des rêves érotiques dingues tout le week-end.
'I had crazy erotic dreams all weekend.' Speakers in French 'make dreams' instead of 'having' them, stacking 'erotic' and slangy 'crazy' afterward.
Pas moi.
'Not me.' Pairing the second half of the negative with stressed 'me' builds the crisp two-word reply 'not me' in French.
Pourquoi tu n'es pas venu à la fête?
'Why didn't you come to the party?' Because Gabriel is male, 'come' stays bare with no extra '-e' after 'are not' in French.
J'avais des obligations personnelles.
'I had some personal obligations.' Here 'I had' sets the ongoing past background for an excuse in French, paired with two clear cognates in reverse order.
Des obligations personnelles un dimanche soir?
'Personal obligations on a Sunday evening?' Saying 'a Sunday evening' needs no 'on' preposition in French, and weekday names stay lowercase.
Une affaire urgente avec un talent.
'An urgent matter with a talent.' Showbiz insiders call a client or star 'a talent', while 'affair' simply means an 'issue' or 'matter' here in French.
Salut tout le monde. Ça va, Marteau?
'Hello everyone. How are you, Marteau?' Arlette teases Andrea with an office nickname that literally means 'hammer'—a playful pun on her surname Martel!
Ça va très bien!
'I am doing very well!' Literally 'that goes very well!', this upbeat four-word response answers 'how's it going?' without ever mentioning 'I' in French.
Et pour Aymeline Val aussi!
'And for Aymeline Val too!' Framing good news with 'and for ... also!' smoothly extends a success to someone else in French.
C'était pas dingue ce projet?
'Wasn't that project crazy?' Dropping the first negative piece in speech makes 'it was not crazy, this project?' a lively way to invite agreement in French.
C'était dingue!
'It was crazy!' You'll hear that punchy slang term meaning 'crazy' or 'wild' everywhere in Paris whenever something turns out thrilling.
Au moins, tout le monde est là ce matin.

'At least everyone is here this morning.' Literally 'at the less', that two-word opener is a handy chunk meaning 'at least' in French. Now let's listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.
Bonjour, Arlette.
Bonjour, Andréa. Tu as bien dormi?
Arlette, cette herbe est terrible.
J'ai fait des rêves érotiques dingues tout le week-end.
Pas moi.
Pourquoi tu n'es pas venu à la fête?
J'avais des obligations personnelles.
Des obligations personnelles un dimanche soir?
Une affaire urgente avec un talent.
Salut tout le monde. Ça va, Marteau?
Ça va très bien!
Et pour Aymeline Val aussi!
C'était pas dingue ce projet?
C'était dingue!
Au moins, tout le monde est là ce matin.
After an intense weekend for all the agents, the team reunites at ASK ready to tackle new challenges together. See you next time!
Au revoir!
